classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: absorbed_wave_power
items.description: Net electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly from coherent waves to a selected plasma particle population, integrated over the plasma volume and resolved by species or charge state.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the net rate at which coherent electromagnetic waves transfer energy directly to selected plasma particles. The selected population may be electrons, ions, or a specified ion charge state, with the result integrated over the plasma volume.

$$
P_{\rm abs} = \left.\frac{dE_{\rm particles}}{dt}\right|_{\rm waves}
$$

where $P_{\rm abs}$ is absorbed wave power, $E_{\rm particles}$ is the energy of the selected particle population, and the subscript “waves” restricts the energy-transfer rate to direct coupling from the electromagnetic wave field. This is the absorbed component of [wave power](name:wave_power), distinct from electromagnetic power that remains carried by the wave.

The quantity includes direct wave-to-particle transfer and excludes subsequent collisional redistribution between particle populations. Species-resolved and charge-state-resolved instances include [electron absorbed wave power](name:thermal_electron_absorbed_power) and ion charge-state absorbed wave power.

items.name: breakdown_magnetic_field
items.description: Breakdown magnetic-field strength associated with local magnetic induction during plasma initiation, without selecting a particular source contribution or field-strength representation.
items.documentation:
The breakdown magnetic field is the local field-strength characterization of the [magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field) relevant to plasma initiation and electron-avalanche breakdown. It represents the magnetic environment at the evaluation location without selecting a particular external-coil residual, cylindrical component, or magnitude operation.

The quantity is interpreted in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is local to the plasma-initiation setting and carries no implied species, charge-state, spatial integration, or averaging over a region.

This parent is broader than any source-specific or reduction-specific field-strength quantity. It is distinct from the [toroidal magnetic field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field), which is a directional cylindrical projection, and from the full magnetic-induction vector represented by [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field).

The [stray breakdown magnetic field](name:stray_breakdown_magnetic_field) specializes this quantity to the residual field at the plasma position produced by incomplete cancelation of external-coil fields, which can inhibit electron-avalanche breakdown. The related [stray breakdown magnetic field magnitude](name:stray_breakdown_magnetic_field_magnitude) further specifies a magnitude representation of that residual field.

items.name: coolant_volume_of_breeder_blanket
items.description: Total geometric volume occupied by lead-lithium coolant/breeder throughout the breeder blanket assembly, excluding external coolant loops and other blanket materials.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the total volume occupied by the lead-lithium coolant/breeder constituent within the complete breeder blanket assembly. It is a material-specific component of the broader volume of breeder blanket and is distinct from the volume of an individual module or layer.

$$
V_{\mathrm{PbLi}} = \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{blanket}}} \chi_{\mathrm{PbLi}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{PbLi}}$ is the PbLi volume, $\Omega_{\mathrm{blanket}}$ is the volume of the complete breeder blanket assembly, $\chi_{\mathrm{PbLi}}$ is one inside the PbLi region and zero elsewhere, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is an elemental volume. The integral excludes external coolant loops, structural materials, voids, and other non-PbLi constituents.

items.name: current_of_correction_coil
items.description: Signed conventional current circulating through a non-axisymmetric correction-coil winding and determining its electromagnetic excitation.
items.documentation:
Correction-coil current is the signed rate of charge transport through the winding circuit. It represents the net circuit current driving the magnetic field generated by the correction coil, rather than the local current density within its conductor.

The current is defined by

$$
I = \frac{dQ}{dt}
$$

where $I$ is conventional current, $Q$ is transported electric charge in coulombs, and $t$ is time in seconds. Its electrical behavior is related to the coil's [resistance](name:resistance_of_correction_coil), while the conductor geometry is characterized by its [cross-sectional area](name:area_of_correction_coil). It is distinct from [passive-loop current](name:current_of_passive_loop), which is induced in a passive conducting loop rather than deliberately driven through a correction-coil winding.

Sign convention: Positive when conventional current flows in the designated positive direction around the correction-coil winding; reversing the winding traversal reverses the sign.

items.name: density_at_pedestal_top
items.description: Local number density of a selected plasma population, including free electrons, ionized species, or an effective fuel species, at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge pedestal.
items.documentation:
Local number density at the H-mode edge pedestal top is the concentration of one selected plasma species or effective pseudo-species at the core-side shoulder of the transport barrier. It is not a sum over different species.

The local number density is defined by

$$
n_s(\mathbf{x}_{\rm pt}) = \lim_{\Delta V \to 0} \frac{\Delta N_s(\mathbf{x}_{\rm pt},\Delta V)}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n_s$ is the local number density of population $s$, $\mathbf{x}_{\rm pt}$ is the position at the pedestal top, $\Delta V$ is a volume surrounding that position, and $\Delta N_s$ is the number of particles of population $s$ within that volume.

For an ion species, the density is the sum $n_s = \sum_z n_{s,z}$ over all represented positive ionic charge states, where $z$ is the ionic charge state and $n_{s,z}$ is the density in that state; neutral atoms are excluded. The electron instance counts free electrons, while the deuterium-tritium instance treats the fuel mixture as one effective pseudo-species. The quantity is local and is not line-, surface-, or volume-averaged. The pedestal-top location is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).

Species-specific instances include [hydrogen density at the pedestal top](name:hydrogen_density_at_pedestal_top) and [electron density at the pedestal top](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_top). Unlike [normalized ion species number density](name:normalized_ion_species_number_density), this quantity is an absolute local density rather than a density divided by a reference value, and unlike [fast ion density](name:fast_ion_density), it is not restricted to a fast nonthermal population.

items.name: effective_electron_diffusivity
items.description: Directional electron particle diffusion coefficient linking a direction-specific effective diffusive electron particle flux to the electron density gradient in a magnetized plasma.
items.documentation:
Effective electron diffusivity is an effective scalar transport coefficient for diffusive electron-particle transport along a specified transport direction in a magnetized plasma. It is the direction-specific coefficient appearing in a macroscopic particle-transport closure for electrons.

The directional constitutive relation is

$$
\Gamma_{e,\alpha}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{e,\alpha}^{\mathrm{eff}}\,\nabla_\alpha n_e
$$

where $\alpha$ labels the specified oriented transport direction, $\Gamma_{e,\alpha}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the component of the diffusive electron particle-flux vector along that direction, $D_{e,\alpha}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective electron diffusivity for the same direction, $\nabla_\alpha n_e$ is the component of the gradient of electron number density along $\alpha$, and $n_e$ is electron number density. The minus sign denotes down-gradient diffusive transport when $D_{e,\alpha}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is positive.

This quantity applies to electron particles in the magnetized plasma and has no isotope or charge-state aggregation. It describes the diffusive contribution only and excludes convective particle fluxes, particle sources, and sinks; the qualifier effective identifies a reduced coefficient for the represented diffusive flux component, not a microscopic collision-only diffusion coefficient or a species-independent particle diffusivity.

This is the effective branch of electron diffusivity. The directional specialization [radial effective electron diffusivity](name:radial_effective_electron_diffusivity) is the specialization for the $\hat R$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: effective_ion_diffusivity
items.description: Effective ion diffusivity is the vector of directional effective Fickian coefficients for particle transport of the ion population summed over all charge states. A positive component corresponds to diffusive ion flux opposite to the total-ion density gradient in the same resolved direction.
items.documentation:
Effective ion diffusivity is the vector of directional effective Fickian coefficients for particle transport of the ion population summed over all charge states. Each component relates the diffusive total-ion particle flux projected along one resolved physical direction to the physical gradient of the total ion number density along that direction.

The component definition is

$$
\Gamma_{i,a}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,a}^{\mathrm{eff}}\left(\hat{e}_a \cdot \nabla n_i\right)
$$

where $a$ labels one resolved physical direction, $\hat{e}_a$ is the normalized direction vector, $D_{i,a}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the corresponding effective ion diffusivity component, $\Gamma_{i,a}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive total-ion particle flux component, and $n_i$ is the total ion number density. The projection $\hat{e}_a \cdot \nabla n_i$ is the metric-scaled physical gradient along $a$, not a bare derivative with respect to a coordinate label.

The charge-state aggregation is defined through the flux-gradient relation: $n_i$ and $\Gamma_{i,a}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ are sums over all ion charge states before the effective coefficient is formed. Therefore $D_{i,a}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is not generally a density-weighted mean of [charge-state-resolved ion diffusivities](name:ion_charge_state_diffusivity). The quantity includes only the diffusive, gradient-driven coefficient; it excludes advective or convective particle transport, source terms, and off-diagonal cross-gradient elements of a rank-two tensor. Concrete directional specializations of this effective quantity include [radial effective ion diffusivity](name:radial_effective_ion_diffusivity); related non-effective ion diffusivity is not a specialization of this effective parent.

Sign convention: Positive when the diffusive ion particle flux component is opposite to the total-ion density gradient along the same resolved direction.

items.name: electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the diffusive thermal energy flux of the electron population to the local electron temperature gradient, serving as the direction-agnostic parent over its radial and poloidal component forms.
items.documentation:
The electron energy diffusion coefficient $D_{e,E}$ quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by the electron population, providing the Fick's-law proportionality between the diffusive electron heat flux and the local electron temperature gradient. It is the electron-species-resolved instance of the parent [energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:energy_diffusion_coefficient) and is distinct from convective or $E \times B$ drift contributions to the total electron heat flux.

The defining relation for the diffusive electron heat flux $\mathbf{Q}_{e,\mathrm{diff}}$ is:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_{e,\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{e,E} \, \nabla T_e
$$

where $D_{e,E}$ is the electron energy diffusion coefficient and $T_e$ is the local electron temperature. In a magnetized plasma $D_{e,E}$ is strongly anisotropic; cross-field radial values govern electron energy confinement while values along field lines are many orders of magnitude larger.

Directional projections of this coefficient include [radial_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient), which governs cross-field energy confinement, and poloidal_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient, which captures transport along the poloidal direction in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. The analogous coefficient for the ion population is given by [ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

items.name: heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description: Positive e-folding distance for the outward decrease of heat-flux magnitude across magnetic flux surfaces in the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the positive cross-field decay length of heat-flux magnitude in the scrape-off layer. It is the heat-flux specialization of [decay length over the scrape-off layer](name:decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer).

For an outward-decreasing heat flux, the defining relation is

$$
\lambda_q = \left|\frac{1}{q}\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}\right|^{-1}
$$

where $\lambda_q$ is the heat-flux decay length, $q$ is the positive heat-flux magnitude of the specified heat channel, and $x$ is outward physical distance across magnetic flux surfaces at the reference location. For exponential falloff, this scale is constant; otherwise it describes the local logarithmic decrease.

The heat channel is not fixed by this parent quantity, and no particular species sum is implied. The [electron heat decay length](name:electron_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer) and [ion heat decay length](name:ion_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer) are its species-resolved specializations.

The divertor-entrance form uses the heat-flux distribution mapped to the outboard midplane, with $x$ and $\lambda_q$ expressed as outboard-midplane distances. In this form, $\lambda_q$ is the upstream exponential decay parameter, distinct from the spreading length $S$, which describes additional broadening of the divertor-target heat-flux distribution. It is not the full width of the broadened target footprint, a density decay length, or a temperature decay length.

items.name: implicit_ion_energy_source_rate
items.description: Implicit ion energy source rate is the coefficient multiplying ion temperature in the stiff, proportional contribution to an ion energy source or sink.
items.documentation:
Implicit ion energy source rate is the proportional coefficient in the stiff part of a decomposed ion energy source or sink. It multiplies the temperature of the ion population whose energy balance is being described.

In the temperature form of that energy balance, the defining decomposition is:

$$
\mathcal{S}_{i,W} = \mathcal{S}_{i,W}^{\mathrm{exp}} + S_{i,W}^{\mathrm{imp}} T_i
$$

where $\mathcal{S}_{i,W}$ is the complete source contribution to the ion-temperature evolution, $\mathcal{S}_{i,W}^{\mathrm{exp}}$ is its explicitly treated remainder, $S_{i,W}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is the implicit coefficient defined here, and $T_i$ is the ion temperature. The subscript $i$ identifies the ion population, and $W$ identifies the energy channel. The decomposition is a linearized representation of the source, not a separation into distinct physical mechanisms.

The coefficient applies to the specified ion population and source contribution; an all-species total is not implied. The [total implicit ion energy source rate](name:total_implicit_ion_energy_source_rate) specializes this quantity to the aggregate ion energy balance, whereas the [implicit ion-state energy source rate](name:implicit_ion_state_energy_source_rate) resolves an individual ion charge state. An aggregate coefficient belongs to the aggregate balance and is not generally an unweighted sum of species coefficients.

This coefficient is not a heating power or power density. Its product with ion temperature gives only the proportional contribution; the explicit remainder must also be included to obtain the complete source or sink.

Sign convention: Positive when the proportional contribution adds energy to the specified ion population, and negative when it removes energy.

items.name: ion_charge_number
items.description: The ionic charge number assigned to one ion species, given by a number-density-weighted mean over all charge states when the distribution is explicit, or by the represented dominant-state or effective charge number otherwise.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the ionic charge number assigned to one ion species. For an explicitly represented charge-state distribution, it is the number-density-weighted mean ionic charge number; a dominant-state representation gives the charge number of that state, while a lumped isonuclear sequence may be represented by an effective charge number.

For an explicitly represented distribution, the species mean is defined by:

$$
\overline{Z}_i = \frac{\sum_q q\,n_{i,q}}{\sum_q n_{i,q}}
$$

Here $i$ identifies the ion species, $q$ is the integer ionic charge number of a charge state, and $n_{i,q}$ is the [ion charge-state density](name:ion_charge_state_density) of species $i$ in state $q$; $\overline{Z}_i$ is the resulting species charge number.

The aggregation is the density-weighted mean over all charge states of this one species. It is not an unweighted average or a sum across distinct ion species; a value restricted to a specified charge-state bundle is [ion charge-state charge number](name:ion_charge_state_charge_number).

For an explicit charge-state distribution, this is the species-specific [average charge number](name:average_charge_number).

items.name: ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Effective coefficient relating density-normalized diffusive energy flux carried by ions to their local temperature gradient, without selecting a transport direction.
items.documentation:
The effective ion energy diffusion coefficient characterizes gradient-driven energy transport carried by a specified ion population. It is the ion-specific specialization of the [energy diffusion coefficient](name:energy_diffusion_coefficient).

For a single-temperature scalar Fickian closure, the defining relation is:

$$
\frac{\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_i} = -D_{i,W}\,\nabla T_i
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive ion thermal-energy flux density, $n_i$ is the number density of the included ions, $D_{i,W}$ is their effective energy diffusion coefficient, and $T_i$ is their energy-valued temperature. The subscript $i$ identifies ions, $W$ identifies the energy channel, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient. For positive diffusivity, the minus sign gives transport down the temperature gradient.

At species scope, the coefficient is a density-weighted mean over all charge states, not a sum of charge-state coefficients. For a collective ion population, this mean extends over all included ion species and charge states. This averaging preserves the displayed flux relation when the constituent populations share the temperature gradient. The [ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) instead resolves one specified charge state.

The quantity selects neither a spatial region nor a transport direction; this does not require isotropic transport. The [parallel specialization](name:parallel_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) selects transport along the magnetic field. The [thermal-ion specialization](name:thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) restricts the carrier population, while the [total-ion specialization](name:total_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) specifies total ion-energy aggregation.

Convective and advective energy fluxes are excluded from the diffusive contribution. The coefficient is distinct from particle diffusion and from thermal conductivity, which relates heat flux directly to a temperature gradient without density normalization.

items.name: ion_particle_diffusivity
items.description: Effective coefficient relating aggregate charged-ion transport to ion-number-density gradients, with directional projections represented by more specific quantities.
items.documentation:
Ion particle diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient for particle spreading driven by an ion-number-density gradient. It is the ion-population component of [particle diffusivity](name:particle_diffusivity), with directional projections represented by quantities such as [radial ion particle diffusivity](name:radial_ion_particle_diffusivity).

For a resolved physical direction $i$, the diffusive ion-particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{ion},i}=-D_{\mathrm{ion},i}\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{ion}}}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{ion},i}$ is the ion-particle flux component, $D_{\mathrm{ion},i}$ is the corresponding particle diffusivity component, $n_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the aggregate ion number density, and $x_i$ is the physical coordinate along the resolved transport direction.

The aggregate coefficient describes the total charged-ion population rather than a selected ion charge state. For charge-state aggregation, it is the density-weighted effective diffusivity over the included charged-ion states, not a sum of state-resolved diffusivities.

items.name: ion_state_mean_ionisation_potential
items.description: Concentration-weighted mean cumulative ionization energy required to reach the charge states represented in a charge-state bundle of one ion species from the neutral ground state.
items.documentation:
Ion-state mean ionization potential is the concentration-weighted mean cumulative ionization energy of an ion charge-state bundle. For each represented charge state, the cumulative energy is the sum of successive ionization energies needed to reach it from the neutral ground state of the same species.

The mean cumulative ionization energy is defined by:

$$
\bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s} = \sum_{z\in\mathcal{B}_s} x_z \left(\sum_{k=0}^{z-1} I_k\right)
$$

where $\bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s}$ is the mean for bundle $s$, $\mathcal{B}_s$ is the set of charge numbers represented in that bundle, $z$ is a represented ionic charge number, and $x_z$ is the relative number concentration of charge state $z$ within the bundle. The fractions satisfy $x_z\geq 0$ and $\sum_{z\in\mathcal{B}_s}x_z=1$. The index $k$ labels an intermediate charge number, and $I_k$ is the ground-state ionization energy required to remove an electron from charge state $k$ and produce charge state $k+1$; the cumulative sum for the neutral state is zero.

The quantity is a density-weighted mean over the charge states represented in the bundle of one ion species, not necessarily over every charge state of that species. It is a mean per particle, not an energy summed over the bundle population; for a bundle containing one charge state, it equals that state's cumulative ionization energy, not the threshold for its next ionization step. It excludes thermal internal energy, excitation energy, radiation losses, and kinetic energy exchanged during ionization or recombination. The [maximum ion charge number](name:ion_state_maximum_charge_number) identifies the highest charge state included in the bundle.

The [change in ion-state mean ionization potential] is the value of this bundle mean after a specified state change minus its value before the change.

items.name: net_power_of_plant_system
items.description: Net real electrical power of a plant system, defined as generation minus internal electrical consumption at the same system boundary; positive values denote net export.
items.documentation:
Net power of a plant system is the real electrical power balance of one plant system, with generation counted positively and internal consumption counted negatively. It is the generated-minus-consumed counterpart to the load-oriented [power of a plant system](name:power_of_plant_system), rather than thermal, apparent, reactive, or accumulated energy.

For a consistently defined system boundary, the net power is defined as

$$
P_\mathrm{net} = P_\mathrm{generated} - P_\mathrm{consumed} = -P_\mathrm{system}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{net}$ is this plant-system quantity, $P_\mathrm{generated}$ is real electrical power generated within the boundary, $P_\mathrm{consumed}$ is real electrical power consumed within the boundary, and $P_\mathrm{system}$ is [power of a plant system](name:power_of_plant_system) using the load-positive convention. Internal transfers between included subsystems cancel. The quantity is the negative of net absorbed power of a plant system when both use the same boundary and scope; positive values denote net electrical export from the system boundary.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_convection_velocity
items.description: Neutral-internal-state convection velocity is the effective vector velocity that parameterizes nondiffusive advection of the number density of a specified neutral internal state. Its resolved components multiply that state density in the corresponding particle flux.
items.documentation:
Neutral-internal-state convection velocity is the effective vector transport coefficient for nondiffusive advection of particles in a specified neutral internal state. It is scoped to neutral-internal-state particle transport and is not a fully species-independent convection velocity.

The convective particle flux associated with this coefficient is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{conv}}_a = n_a \mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{conv}}_a
$$

where $a$ identifies the specified neutral internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{conv}}_a$ is its convective particle flux, $n_a$ is its number density, and $\mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{conv}}_a$ is the neutral-internal-state convection velocity.

This parent quantity denotes the full vector concept; component-resolved quantities such as the [poloidal neutral-internal-state convection velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_convection_velocity) are projections of the same neutral-internal-state transport coefficient, not changes of species scope. It excludes diffusive transport coefficients, bulk neutral flow velocity unless that is explicitly the coefficient used in the convective flux relation, and convection velocities for charged-particle species.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component of $\mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{conv}}_a$ points in the positive sense of the component direction named by the resolved standard name.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_source_rate
items.description: Neutral internal-state source rate is the flux-surface-averaged net particle gain or loss per volume in one specified internal state of a neutral species.
items.documentation:
Neutral internal-state source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which particles enter or leave one specified internal state of a neutral species. It supplies the source term in the particle-number density transport equation for that state.

The net source rate is defined by

$$
S_{0,a}(\psi)=\left\langle S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{gain}}-S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{loss}}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $S_{0,a}$ is the neutral internal-state source rate, $S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{gain}}$ and $S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{loss}}$ are the local particle addition and removal rates per volume for the included processes, $0$ denotes electrical neutrality, $a$ identifies the internal state, $\psi$ labels a magnetic flux surface, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes a flux-surface average.

This quantity applies to one neutral species and one specified internal state; it is not summed over internal states and excludes charged-particle populations. Internal-state resolution distinguishes populations within the electrically neutral species, not different ionic charge states. The source rate is not the full time derivative of the state density, because spatial transport also changes that density.

Summing these rates over a complete set of internal states, for the same included processes, gives the [neutral source rate](name:neutral_source_rate). Transfers solely between internal states cancel in that sum, although they contribute gains and losses to individual state equations.

Sign convention: Positive when the included processes produce a net gain of particles in the specified neutral internal state; negative values indicate net removal.

items.name: neutral_particle_diffusivity
items.description: Effective coefficient relating neutral-particle transport to neutral number-density gradients, with components resolved along the relevant transport directions.
items.documentation:
Neutral particle diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient for particle spreading driven by a neutral number-density gradient. It is the neutral-population specialization of [particle diffusivity](name:particle_diffusivity), without selecting a transport direction.

For each resolved direction $i$, the diffusive neutral-particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_i^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_i\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{n}}}{\partial s_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_i^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive neutral-particle flux component, $D_i$ is the corresponding component of neutral particle diffusivity, $n_{\mathrm{n}}$ is neutral particle number density, and $s_i$ is physical arclength along the resolved direction. The minus sign specifies transport down the number-density gradient.

This parent covers directional components such as [parallel neutral particle diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_particle_diffusivity) and [poloidal neutral particle diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_diffusivity). It does not select a particular neutral chemical species or internal state; those population refinements are represented by [neutral species particle diffusivity](name:neutral_species_particle_diffusivity).

items.name: neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity
items.description: Effective advective velocity vector relating the number density of a neutral species in a specified internal state to its convective particle flux in edge plasma.
items.documentation:
Neutral-state particle convection velocity is the effective vector coefficient of the density-proportional advective particle flux for a specified internal state of a neutral species in the edge plasma. It describes directed transport after density-gradient-driven diffusion has been separated.

The convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{n,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_{n,a}\mathbf{v}_{n,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $a$ labels the selected internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{n,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is that state's convective neutral-particle flux, $n_{n,a}$ is its neutral-particle number density, and $\mathbf{v}_{n,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this convection velocity.

The population includes thermal and nonthermal particles of the selected neutral state; no sum or average over internal states or species is implied. The quantity excludes density-gradient-driven diffusive transport, describes particle transport rather than heat or momentum transport, and need not equal the bulk neutral-flow velocity. Unlike [ion-charge-state particle convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_particle_convection_velocity), it resolves neutral internal states rather than ionic charge states.

No directional projection is imposed on this vector. The [poloidal neutral-state particle convection velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity) is its poloidal projection, while the [parallel neutral-state particle convection velocity](name:parallel_neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity) is its projection along the magnetic-field direction. Both retain the same neutral-state population and particle-transport scope.

items.name: neutral_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Effective convection velocity assigned to the diamagnetic contribution to neutral-species momentum transport, retaining the direction of transport.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective convection-velocity vector assigned to the diamagnetic contribution to momentum transport of a selected neutral species. It is a transport coefficient, not an intrinsic magnetic drift of electrically neutral particles.

Its role in a convective momentum closure is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{conv}}_{P_0,*}=P_0\mathbf{v}_{0,*}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{0,*}$ is the effective diamagnetic convection velocity, $P_0$ is the transported component of neutral-species momentum density, and $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{conv}}_{P_0,*}$ is the corresponding diamagnetic contribution to its convective momentum flux. The subscript $0$ denotes the neutral population, and the asterisk labels the diamagnetic contribution. The transported momentum component and the direction of its transport are distinct.

The coefficient applies to one neutral species without resolving its internal states, unlike the [neutral-state velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It is not a sum over different neutral species and excludes ionic charge states.

The parent [velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:perpendicular_ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) establishes the pressure-gradient-associated attribution. For neutrals, that attribution denotes an effective transport contribution; the charged-particle diamagnetic drift formula does not apply because the particle charge is zero. This coefficient is distinct from the total neutral bulk-flow velocity.

The [neutral velocity magnitude due to diamagnetic drift] is the Euclidean norm of this vector and therefore omits its transport direction.

Sign convention: Positive when a component of the effective convection velocity points along its specified positive transport direction.

items.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
items.description: Parallel current density due to heat viscosity is the signed charge flux along the local magnetic field generated by heat-viscosity stresses in a collisional magnetized plasma.
items.documentation:
Parallel current density due to heat viscosity is the local magnetic-field-aligned component of the electric-current contribution generated by heat-viscosity stresses in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure.

Its defining projection is

$$
j_{\parallel} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $j_{\parallel}$ is this signed parallel current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the [heat-viscosity current-density vector](name:current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field. Specifically, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, where $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its nonzero magnitude.

This quantity is the net conventional charge flux attributed to heat viscosity in the edge plasma, combining the charged-species contributions rather than selecting one species. It is a local signed component, not a current magnitude, a flux-surface average, or the total current density from all mechanisms.

The [vertical heat-viscosity current density](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity) is a different projection of the same parent vector. By contrast, [parallel current density due to parallel viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) has the same projection direction but represents a distinct viscous-stress contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when the heat-viscosity contribution to conventional electric current flows along the local magnetic field.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description: Projection along the local magnetic field of the E×B guiding-center drift for one ion charge state in the edge plasma, identically zero for the ideal drift.
items.documentation:
The parallel component of the [ion charge-state E×B drift velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is its signed projection along the local magnetic-field direction.

For the ideal E×B drift, the defining projection is

$$
v_{E,\parallel} = \mathbf{v}_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2} = 0.
$$

Here $v_{E,\parallel}$ is the parallel drift component for the specified ion charge state, $\mathbf{v}_E$ is its E×B guiding-center drift velocity, $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector directed along the magnetic field. The definition requires a nonzero magnetic field.

This quantity applies locally to one specified charge state of one ion species in the magnetized edge plasma; it is neither summed nor averaged over charge states or species. The ideal E×B drift is independent of ion mass and charge for fixed local fields. This component does not denote the total parallel ion velocity, and contributions from other mechanisms are excluded.

Unlike the [toroidal component](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), which need not vanish, the field-aligned component vanishes identically because the ideal E×B drift is perpendicular to the local magnetic field.

items.name: parallel_net_ion_momentum_source
items.description: Area-normalized net rate of ion momentum transfer along the local magnetic field, summed algebraically over all ionic charge states and contributing source and sink processes.
items.documentation:
The parallel net ion momentum source is the area-normalized net rate of [momentum](name:momentum) transfer to the ion population along the local magnetic field. It retains the sign of the transfer rather than representing its magnitude.

Its defining projection is

$$
S_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{net}} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf S_i^{\mathrm{net}}
$$

where $S_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{net}}$ is this parallel source, $\mathbf S_i^{\mathrm{net}}$ is the vector [net ion momentum source](name:net_ion_momentum_source), and the subscript $i$ identifies the ion population. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ points along the local magnetic field $\mathbf B$; the projection is defined where that field is nonzero.

The source is summed over all ionic charge states of the ion population and all contributing physical processes, combining opposing transfers algebraically rather than summing their magnitudes. It excludes the [neutral momentum source](name:neutral_momentum_source), although interactions with neutrals can contribute momentum transfer to ions. It is a source term in the ion momentum balance, not a [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux) describing transport across an oriented surface.

Sign convention: Positive when the net momentum transfer to ions points along the local magnetic field.

items.name: parallel_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Field-aligned projection of the effective diamagnetic pressure-gradient velocity contribution assigned to one internal state of a neutral species in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The parallel neutral-state velocity due to diamagnetic drift is the field-aligned projection of an effective pressure-gradient transport contribution assigned to one neutral atomic or molecular internal quantum state in the edge plasma. It represents an effective fluid contribution, not a direct magnetic drift of individual neutral particles.

For the selected neutral state, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\mathrm{dia},s,\parallel} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},s}^{\mathrm{eff}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $s$ labels the selected internal state of the specified neutral species, $v_{\mathrm{dia},s,\parallel}$ is its parallel velocity contribution, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},s}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is its effective diamagnetic pressure-gradient velocity contribution, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

The quantity is state resolved, with no sum or average over internal states or neutral species. It excludes independent parallel-flow contributions and is not the total [bulk neutral internal-state velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity). Because neutral particles carry no charge, the charged-particle diamagnetic-drift formula does not directly define this effective neutral contribution.

This quantity is the field-parallel specialization of [neutral-state velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), whereas [perpendicular neutral-state velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:perpendicular_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) selects a direction perpendicular to the magnetic field. If the assigned effective contribution is purely perpendicular, its parallel projection is zero.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective neutral-state velocity contribution has a component along the local magnetic-field vector.

items.name: plasma_energy
items.description: Plasma energy is the volume-integrated internal kinetic energy carried by all confined electron and ion populations, including thermal and suprathermal particles. It excludes electromagnetic-field, rest-mass, and organized bulk-flow energy.
items.documentation:
Plasma energy is the volume-integrated internal kinetic energy carried by all confined electron and ion populations, including thermal and suprathermal populations. It is the all-population stored particle energy of the confined plasma, not a thermal-only component.

A pressure-tensor definition gives the stored particle energy without assuming isotropic distributions:

$$
W_\mathrm{p} = \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} \sum_a \frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{Tr}\mathbf{P}_a\, dV
$$

where $W_\mathrm{p}$ is the plasma energy, $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, $a$ labels the electron, ion, and modeled suprathermal populations included in the confined plasma, $\mathbf{P}_a$ is the pressure tensor of population $a$ in its local mean-flow frame, and $dV$ is the scalar volume element. For isotropic populations this reduces to the pressure-sum relation with energy density $3p_\mathrm{tot}/2$, where $p_\mathrm{tot}=\sum_a p_a$; for a gyrotropic anisotropic population the contribution is $p_{\perp a}+p_{\parallel a}/2$.

This quantity excludes electromagnetic-field energy, electrostatic-field energy, rest-mass energy, and organized macroscopic bulk-flow energy. [Electron energy](name:volume_integrated_square_of_poloidal_magnetic_field), [thermal plasma energy](name:thermal_plasma_energy), and [fast-particle energy](name:fast_particle_energy) are component contributions, while total plasma energy and total particle energy denote the corresponding all-population stored particle-energy concept when the naming emphasizes totality.

items.name: poloidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam
items.description: Poloidal angle of the electron-cyclotron beam's mean propagation direction, measured from inward horizontal toward downward.
items.documentation:
Poloidal angle of electron cyclotron beam

For the beam mean wave vector, the steering angle is defined by

$$\theta = \operatorname{atan2}(Z_{\mathrm{axis}} - Z,\; R - R_{\mathrm{axis}})$$

where $\theta$ is this beam direction angle, $k_R$ is the [radial wave-vector component], and $k_Z$ is the [vertical wave-vector component](name:vertical_wave_vector_of_beam_tracing_beam), with components taken along the $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{Z}$ directions. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; $\operatorname{atan2}(y,x)$ returns the quadrant-resolved angle for the ordered pair $(x,y)$.

The quantity applies to one electron-cyclotron beam's mean wave vector at the location where its angle is defined; it is not an aggregate across beams or an average of individual ray angles. Unlike [poloidal angle of a beam-tracing beam](name:poloidal_angle_of_beam_tracing_beam), it describes propagation direction rather than the angular position of trajectory points. Its reference direction is inward, rather than the magnetic-axis-referenced position angle described by [poloidal angle]. Poloidal steering contributes to the radial deposition location but is not itself a deposition-position coordinate.

It complements the [toroidal angle of the electron-cyclotron beam](name:toroidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam), which describes the toroidal component of the beam steering direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the projected mean propagation direction is rotated from inward $-\hat{R}$ toward downward $-\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: radial_coordinate
items.description: Major-radius coordinate of a geometric point or reference position, equal to its perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Major-radius coordinate of a geometric point or reference position is its perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal coordinates of the same point in the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame, with $z$ the vertical coordinate along the same axis as $Z$.

This coordinate applies to plasma positions and device geometry. It is nonnegative and vanishes on the toroidal symmetry axis; it is distinct from a minor-radius distance measured from the magnetic axis and from a magnetic flux label. No summation, averaging, or weighting is implied by the general coordinate; specialized quantities define their reference positions or aggregation conventions.

For example, the [radial coordinate of a conductor cross-section](name:radial_coordinate_of_conductor_cross_section) locates its geometric center, whereas the [radial coordinate of the current center](name:radial_coordinate_of_current_center) is the toroidal-current-weighted mean major radius over the plasma cross-section.

items.name: radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Effective kinematic diffusion coefficient for redistribution of the major-radius momentum component carried by ions of one specified species and charge state.
items.documentation:
The radial ion charge-state momentum diffusion coefficient governs diffusive redistribution of the major-radius component of [momentum](name:momentum) carried by ions of one specified species and charge state. The major-radius direction is the direction of increasing $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

In a local kinematic Fick-law closure, the diffusive flux across an oriented surface is:

$$
\Pi_{s,R}^{\rm diff} = -m_s n_s D_{s,R}\,\hat{\mathbf n}\cdot\nabla v_{s,R}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state, $\Pi_{s,R}^{\rm diff}$ is the flux of major-radius momentum across the surface, $m_s$ is the ion mass, $n_s$ is the charge-state number density, $D_{s,R}$ is this diffusion coefficient, $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the surface's oriented unit normal, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator, and $v_{s,R}$ is the charge-state mean velocity component along increasing major radius.

Radial identifies the transported momentum component, not the direction across which momentum is transported. In particular, the major-radius direction is not generally normal to a magnetic flux surface. The coefficient is charge-state resolved, with no sum or average over charge states implied, and excludes convective momentum transport, nondiffusive residual stress, and external momentum sources.

This quantity specializes the [momentum diffusion coefficient](name:momentum_diffusion_coefficient) to a specified ion charge state and major-radius momentum component. The [parallel ion charge-state momentum diffusion coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) is the corresponding specialization for the field-parallel momentum component.

items.name: radial_ion_energy_convection_velocity
items.description: Effective radial transport velocity for convective ion-energy transport in the edge plasma; it need not equal the radial ion particle-flow velocity.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective velocity assigned to the convective component of ion-energy transport in the edge plasma. It parameterizes energy advection and is not, by definition, the ion particle-flow velocity.

Its defining relation to the convective ion-energy flux is

$$
u_{i,E,r}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \frac{Q_{i,E,r}^{\mathrm{conv}}}{W_{i,E}}$$

where $Q_{i,E,r}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial convective ion-energy flux and $W_{i,E}$ is the corresponding ion-energy density. The quantity is defined where $W_{i,E}$ is nonzero and excludes diffusive, conductive, and source contributions. It is the radial component of ion_energy_convection_velocity, and differs from [radial_ion_convection_velocity](name:radial_ion_particle_convection_velocity), which parameterizes particle transport.

Sign convention: Positive when the associated convective ion-energy flux points in the $+\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: radial_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Fickian diffusion coefficient for radial transport of thermal energy by the aggregated neutral particle population in an edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The radial neutral energy diffusion coefficient characterizes the proportionality between the radial diffusive neutral thermal-energy flux and the major-radius gradient of neutral thermal-energy density in an edge plasma. Neutral transport is not constrained to magnetic-field lines, and this coefficient is the radial component of the directionally resolved neutral transport.

The Fickian closure is

$$
q_{n,R}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{n,R}^{E}\frac{\partial}{\partial R}\left(\frac{3}{2}n_n T_n\right)
$$

where $q_{n,R}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the radial diffusive neutral thermal-energy flux, $D_{n,R}^{E}$ is this radial diffusion coefficient, $R$ is the major-radius coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $n_n$ is neutral number density, and $T_n$ is neutral temperature.

This coefficient is the radial component of the parent [neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and applies to the aggregated neutral population. Directional comparison is provided by the [poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient), while state-resolved transport is represented by [radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

items.name: radial_total_ion_energy_flux
items.description: Total ion energy flux across magnetic flux surfaces is the net outward energy transport per unit area, averaged over each surface and summed over all ion species and charge states.
items.documentation:
Total ion energy flux across magnetic flux surfaces represents the surface-averaged transport of energy carried by the aggregate ion population. It includes conductive thermal-energy transport and convective enthalpy or bulk-kinetic transport.

The defining surface average is:

$$
\Gamma_{i,W}^{\mathrm{out}} = \frac{\int_S \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{i,W}^{\mathrm{tot}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}\,dA}{\int_S dA}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,W}^{\mathrm{out}}$ is the surface-averaged outward ion energy flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{i,W}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the [total ion energy-flux vector](name:total_ion_energy_flux), $S$ is the magnetic flux surface, $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is its outward unit normal, and $dA$ is a surface-area element. The subscripts $i$ and $W$ identify the ion population and energy channel, respectively.

The aggregation is a sum over all ion species and charge states, not a density-weighted mean. The [ion charge-state energy flux](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux) instead restricts transport to one specified charge state. Electron and neutral energy transport are excluded. Surface averaging preserves a flux density; integrating the normal flux over the surface instead gives the energy-transfer rate through that surface.

The magnetic-surface-normal projection is distinct from the major-radius projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Sign convention: Positive when net ion energy transport is outward through the magnetic flux surface, toward increasing enclosed volume.

items.name: straight_field_line_angle
items.description: An angular coordinate that labels position along magnetic field lines after a straight-field-line transformation, making field-line trajectories linear on each magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
A straight-field-line angle is an angular coordinate for labeling position along magnetic field lines in a magnetic-flux coordinate description. The transformation is chosen so that field-line trajectories are straight, or have constant angular slope, on each flux surface.

This quantity denotes the coordinate itself rather than a mechanical steering angle, wave phase, or physical distance along a field line. Its origin, angular orientation, and selected angular direction are defined by the associated straight-field-line coordinate convention.

The [poloidal straight-field-line angle] is the poloidal specialization of this general coordinate concept. Other specializations, when defined, differ by the angular direction or coordinate convention rather than by a different underlying physical quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when position advances in the defined positive direction of the straight-field-line angular coordinate.

items.name: thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Signed local rate of Coulomb-collisional energy transfer from nonthermal particles to bulk thermal electrons, including all source-particle orbit classes.
items.documentation:
Thermal-electron collisional power density is the local rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from designated nonthermal particle distributions to bulk thermal electrons. It includes all guiding-center orbit classes of the source particles and is a source or sink of electron energy, not stored electron energy.

The transfer is defined by the kinetic-energy moment of the collision operator acting on the thermal electrons:

$$
P_e^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_a \int \varepsilon_e(\mathbf{p})\,C_{ea}[f_e,f_a](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{p})\,d^3p
$$

where $P_e^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the thermal-electron collisional power density, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $\mathbf{p}$ is electron momentum, and $\varepsilon_e$ is electron kinetic energy. The function $f_e$ is the thermal-electron momentum distribution, $f_a$ is a designated nonthermal source distribution labeled by $a$, and $C_{ea}$ is the Coulomb-collisional time derivative of $f_e$ caused by interactions with $f_a$. The integral covers all electron momenta; the sum superposes the designated nonthermal source populations.

This is the thermal-target specialization of [electron collisional power density](name:electron_power_density_due_to_collisions). It excludes energy delivered to nonthermal electrons and energy transfer by noncollisional mechanisms. For energy-conserving binary collisions, the transfer has the opposite sign to the corresponding kinetic-energy change of the nonthermal source particles.

The [co-passing](name:co_passing_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions), [counter-passing](name:counter_passing_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions), and [trapped](name:trapped_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) contributions sum to the orbit-unrestricted transfer when evaluated with the same spatial averaging. These orbit restrictions apply to the nonthermal source particles, not the receiving electrons. The local quantity need not be constant on a magnetic flux surface; a flux-surface-averaged member denotes the average of its corresponding local contribution, and averaging is not intrinsic to this definition.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer net kinetic energy into the bulk thermal-electron population.

items.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized diffusive thermal energy flux of a specified ion charge state to its local temperature gradient, serving as the direction-agnostic parent over directional component forms.
items.documentation:
The ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient $D_{i,z,E}$ quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by ions in a specified charge state $z$, providing the Fick's-law proportionality between the density-normalized diffusive ion heat flux for that charge state and the local ion temperature gradient. It is the charge-state-resolved specialization of the [ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and is distinct from convective, advective, and $E \times B$ contributions to the total ion heat flux.

The defining relation for the density-normalized diffusive energy flux is:

$$
\frac{\mathbf{Q}_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_{i,z}} = -D_{i,z,E}\,\nabla T_{i,z}
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by ions in charge state $z$, $n_{i,z}$ is their number density, and $T_{i,z}$ is their temperature. The minus sign denotes transport down the local temperature gradient.

This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not summed over charge states. Its directional realizations include the [radial thermal ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:radial_thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient), while the corresponding charge-state-aggregated [ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) represents a density-weighted mean over ion species and charge states.

items.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Signed local rate of Coulomb-collisional energy transfer from fast or non-Maxwellian particles to thermal ions of one specified species and charge state, including all donor orbit classes.
items.documentation:
Thermal-ion charge-state collisional power density is the local rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from a fast or non-Maxwellian particle population to thermal ions of one specified species and charge state. It is an energy-exchange source or sink for the receiving thermal population, not its stored kinetic-energy density.

The receiving population's kinetic-energy moment defines this contribution:

$$
P_{i,z,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{a\in\mathcal{D}} \int \frac{1}{2}m_i v^2 C_{iz,a}\bigl(f_{iz}^{\mathrm{th}},f_a\bigr)(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{i,z,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the thermal-ion charge-state collisional power density at position $\mathbf{x}$, $i$ identifies the receiving ion species, $z$ is its charge number, and $m_i$ is its particle mass. The vector $\mathbf{v}$ is the receiving ion velocity, $v$ is its magnitude, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space integration element. The distribution $f_{iz}^{\mathrm{th}}$ describes the receiving thermal ions, $f_a$ describes donor species $a$, and $\mathcal{D}$ is the set of species in the designated fast or non-Maxwellian donor population. The operator $C_{iz,a}$ gives the collisional time derivative of the receiving distribution caused by Coulomb interactions with that donor species.

The donor contribution includes co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped orbit classes. There is no sum over receiving ion charge states and no orbit-class restriction on the thermal recipients. The local definition imposes no flux-surface averaging. Energy transferred to fast ions or electrons is excluded.

This is the thermal-recipient component of [ion charge-state collisional power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions), rather than the combined thermal- and fast-ion contribution. The donor orbit-class contributions sum to this quantity locally. Flux-surface averaging those contributions gives the corresponding orbit-resolved averages, including [co-passing thermal-ion charge-state collisional power density](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [counter-passing thermal-ion charge-state collisional power density](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions increase the kinetic-energy density of the specified thermal-ion charge-state population.

items.name: thermal_power_of_plant_component_port
items.description: Rate of heat removed from a plant component by coolant, determined by the coolant enthalpy increase between the associated inlet and outlet.
items.documentation:
Thermal power at a plant-component port is the rate of heat energy transferred from the component into the coolant circuit. It is the thermal component of power of a plant component port.

The defining relation is

$$
P_\mathrm{th} = \dot{m}\left(h_\mathrm{out}-h_\mathrm{in}\right)
$$

where $P_\mathrm{th}$ is thermal power, $\dot{m}$ is coolant mass flow rate in kg s$^{-1}$, and $h_\mathrm{in}$ and $h_\mathrm{out}$ are the coolant specific enthalpies at the inlet and outlet in J kg$^{-1}$, respectively.

Positive values mean that the coolant gains enthalpy along the flow path and therefore removes heat from the plant component. This quantity excludes electrical, radiative, and other non-coolant-mediated power transfers.

items.name: toroidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam
items.description: Toroidal angle of an electron-cyclotron beam is the signed inclination of its mean launch direction out of the local poloidal plane.
items.documentation:
Toroidal angle of electron cyclotron beam

The beam steering angle is defined by

$$
\phi_{\mathrm{beam}} = \arcsin\left(\frac{k_\phi}{k}\right)
$$

where $\phi_{\mathrm{beam}}$ is the toroidal steering angle, $k_\phi$ is the toroidal component of the mean launch wave vector, and $k$ is the magnitude of that mean wave vector. The principal inverse-sine branch is used.

This quantity describes the mean launch direction of one beam, not its spatial toroidal position or the [mechanical rotation angle of a launcher mirror](name:angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror). Together with the [poloidal steering angle](name:poloidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam), it specifies the mean launch direction. The resulting wave-vector projection along the local magnetic field determines the magnetic-field-parallel refractive index relevant to [electron-cyclotron-driven current](name:current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive).

Sign convention: Positive when the mean launch wave vector has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal azimuth $\phi$, counterclockwise when viewed from above.

items.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Toroidal directional diffusion coefficient governing diffusive transport of bulk-ion momentum as the toroidal diagonal component of the ion momentum diffusivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal ion momentum diffusion coefficient is the toroidal directional component of the [ion momentum diffusion coefficient](name:ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) vector and the $\hat{\phi}\hat{\phi}$ diagonal component of the bulk-ion momentum diffusivity tensor. It relates the diffusive flux of charge-state-summed bulk-ion toroidal momentum density along $\hat{\phi}$ to the local gradient of that momentum density along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above along $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

In a gradient-diffusion closure, this diagonal component satisfies:

$$
\Pi_{\phi\phi,i}^{\rm diff} = -\chi_{\phi,i}\,\frac{1}{R}\frac{\partial}{\partial \phi}\left(m_i n_i v_{\phi,i}\right)
$$

where $\Pi_{\phi\phi,i}^{\rm diff}$ is the $\hat{\phi}$ projection of the diffusive flux of bulk-ion toroidal momentum density, positive for transport in the direction of increasing $\phi$; $\chi_{\phi,i}$ is this coefficient; $m_i$ is ion mass; $n_i$ is bulk-ion number density summed over all charge states; and $v_{\phi,i}$ is the density-weighted mean bulk-ion flow velocity component along $\hat{\phi}$ over all charge states, positive in the direction of increasing $\phi$. The derivative is taken at fixed $R$ and $Z$, so $R^{-1}\partial/\partial\phi$ is the directional derivative along $\hat{\phi}$.

The toroidal qualifier denotes the tensor direction of both the transported momentum component and the spatial flux-gradient projection; it is not a cross-flux-surface coefficient for transport of toroidal momentum. This distinguishes it from [toroidal ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), which is charge-state resolved and flux-surface-normal, positive toward increasing flux label. Convective momentum transport, explicit momentum sources or sinks, and residual-stress contributions are excluded.

Sign convention: Positive when a positive derivative of the bulk-ion toroidal momentum density along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ produces a diffusive flux of that momentum in the direction of decreasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: vertical_bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity
items.description: Mean translational velocity of neutral particles in one specified internal quantum or energy state, projected along the toroidal symmetry axis in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the vertical component of the local [bulk neutral internal-state velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity) in the edge plasma. It describes directed motion of a neutral species in one specified quantum or energy state along the toroidal symmetry axis.

The component is the normalized first velocity moment projected onto the vertical direction:

$$
u_{0,a,Z}(\mathbf r)=\hat{\mathbf z}\cdot\mathbf u_{0,a}(\mathbf r)=\frac{\int (\mathbf v\cdot\hat{\mathbf z})f_{0,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_{0,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $u_{0,a,Z}$ is the vertical bulk velocity component, $\mathbf u_{0,a}$ is the corresponding bulk velocity vector, subscript $0$ denotes neutrals, and $a$ identifies the specified internal state. Here $\mathbf r$ is spatial position, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, and $f_{0,a}$ is the phase-space number density of the selected neutral species and state. The integrals extend over all particle velocities. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf z}$ points along increasing vertical height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The averaging is within the specified species and internal state; different internal states and other species are not combined. The velocity is defined where the selected state's number density is nonzero. Bulk denotes mean translational flow, not an additional hot- or cold-population restriction. This component is neither the flow-speed magnitude, a thermal velocity spread, nor a particle flux.

The [radial neutral internal-state velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity) is the distinct major-radius projection of the state-resolved flow; the vertical component instead follows the symmetry-axis direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the neutral internal-state bulk flow has a component toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Signed vertical component of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic fluid velocity for one ion charge state in the edge plasma, distinct from individual guiding-center motion.
items.documentation:
The vertical ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid velocity onto the direction parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis. It applies to one ion charge state in the edge plasma and represents a fluid-moment contribution rather than individual guiding-center motion.

For a specified ion charge state, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\ast\alpha,Z} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\alpha$ identifies the ion species and charge state, $v_{\ast\alpha,Z}$ is its vertical diamagnetic-drift velocity, $p_\alpha$ is its partial pressure, $\nabla p_\alpha$ is its pressure gradient, $q_\alpha$ is its signed particle charge, $n_\alpha$ is its number density, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, and $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ points along increasing vertical height $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $\phi$ is toroidal angle.

This quantity is local and charge-state resolved; it is neither summed nor averaged over charge states. In contrast, the [binormal ion velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:binormal_ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) uses a local binormal projection and a density-weighted mean over ionic charge states.

Only the diamagnetic contribution is included; electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent parallel flow are excluded. The diamagnetic velocity vector is perpendicular to the magnetic field, but its vertical component need not vanish because the vertical direction is not generally field aligned.

Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic fluid velocity has a component toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
items.description: Wave phase at an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the relative angular offset of a coherent radio-frequency excitation at a selected strap or module from a specified reference.
items.documentation:
Wave phase at an ion-cyclotron heating antenna describes the relative phase of a coherent radio-frequency excitation at a selected strap or module. It encompasses feed-voltage phase and inter-element excitation phasing without restricting the excitation to a forward traveling wave or fixing the reference to the first element.

The relative phase is defined by

$$
\varphi_{kr} = \arg\!\left(A_k A_r^*\right) \pmod{2\pi}
$$

where $\varphi_{kr}$ is the wave phase of selected element $k$ relative to reference $r$, $A_k$ is the selected excitation phasor, $A_r$ is the coherent reference phasor, the superscript $*$ denotes complex conjugation, and $\arg$ extracts the complex argument. Phasors use the temporal factor $e^{+\mathrm{i}\omega t}$, where $\mathrm{i}$ is the imaginary unit, $\omega$ is their common angular frequency, and $t$ is time. The phase is defined modulo $2\pi$ and is undefined if either phasor vanishes.

The quantity applies to one specified excitation-reference pair, not a sum or average over antenna elements. For inter-element phasing, the phasors represent the same excitation type at specified reference planes. Relative strap phases shape the launched wave spectrum, but this quantity contains neither excitation amplitude nor power.

The [forward-wave phase](name:forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) specializes this quantity to forward power-wave phasors referenced to the first module. By contrast, the [reflected phase](name:reflected_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) compares reflected and forward waves at the same element rather than excitations at different elements.

Sign convention: Positive when the selected excitation leads its specified reference in phase under the stated temporal convention.
